unit-1.title: Six vowels to start
unit-1.goal: Every Korean syllable needs a vowel. These six are the simplest.
unit-1.body: Hangul is an alphabet, not a set of pictures. There are 40 letters, they were designed to be learned quickly, and you are about to learn six of them.
points: Letters are grouped into square blocks, and each block is one syllable.
A vowel is either a tall line or a flat line — that decides where it sits in the block.
Say each one out loud as you trace it. The sound is half the lesson.

unit-2.title: Your first consonants
unit-2.goal: Five consonants. With the vowels you know, that is already 30 syllables.

unit-3.title: Putting them together
unit-3.goal: Consonant plus vowel makes a block you can read.
unit-3.body: A Korean syllable is written as one square. The consonant goes first — on the left for a tall vowel, on top for a flat one.
points: A tall vowel (ㅏ ㅓ ㅣ) stands to the right of the consonant.
A flat vowel (ㅗ ㅜ ㅡ) lies underneath it.
Read the block the way you would read a page: left to right, then down.

unit-4.title: Five more consonants
unit-4.goal: ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅎ — the rest of the plain series.

unit-5.title: Reading more blocks
unit-5.goal: Including the one letter that makes no sound at all.

unit-6.title: Adding a y sound
unit-6.goal: One extra stroke turns ㅏ into ㅑ. The pattern holds for all four.

unit-7.title: A puff of air
unit-7.goal: ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ are letters you know, with one stroke added.

unit-8.title: The e vowels
unit-8.goal: ㅐ ㅔ ㅒ ㅖ — vowels made by adding ㅣ.

unit-9.title: Doubled and tightened
unit-9.goal: Five letters written twice, said tighter.

unit-10.title: The w vowels
unit-10.goal: Two vowels written as one. The last of the 40 letters.

unit-11.title: A letter at the foot
unit-11.goal: 받침 — the consonant that closes a syllable.
unit-11.body: A block can hold a third letter, underneath the other two. It is called a 받침, and it closes the syllable.
points: The third letter always goes at the bottom of the square.
A 받침 is only ever released as one of seven sounds, whichever letter is written.
This is where most beginners' reading breaks. Take it slowly.

unit-12.title: Reading 한글
unit-12.goal: You now know every letter. Read the name of the writing system itself.

sounds.title: When sounds meet
sounds.blurb: Why 학교 is not said the way it is written.
sounds.intro: You can now read every letter. Korean writes the pieces a word is made of, and changes some of them when they touch — so a few words sound different from how they look. Here are the ones you will meet first.
sounds.note: You do not have to memorise these. Listen for them, and they will start to sound normal.

mistakes.emptyBody: When something slips, it turns up here so you can put it right.
